Subject: Dedicated capacity intake — quick throughput/latency triage

Hi Samir —

Thanks for self-signing up to evaluate Redwood Dedicated. I see Aurora Analytics selected a dedicated capacity trial; I wanted to grab a few quick details so our demo (and the SE time) is focused on your throughput/latency requirements.

Quick ask: could you share target QPS / tokens-per-second and a p95 latency goal? Also, which model(s) are you planning to serve (open model name or LLM provider)?

If you prefer a quick walkthrough instead of back-and-forth, you can pick a 30-min slot here: https://calendly.com/redwood/sdr-dedicated-demo — I’m available next week in PST.

Thanks — happy to loop in Ben (solutions) for a technical deep-dive.

Best,

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — quick throughput/latency triage

Hi Neha —

Thanks — quick answers below so we can get the right folks on the call: 
- Target sustained throughput: ~1,500 tokens/sec (mix of short and mid-length requests)
- Peak bursts: up to ~2,000 tokens/sec for short windows (~1–2 minutes)
- Concurrent requests: targeting ~200 concurrent low-latency requests during business hours
- Latency goal: p95 under 150ms for generation (we can tolerate p99 spikes occasionally)
- Model: planning to serve Llama-2-70B (quantized variant) and evaluate a distilled 13B for lower-cost paths

Timezone: PST (San Francisco). Best times next week: Tue/Wed mornings.

Let me know if Ben needs any additional profiling data — I can pull sequence-length distributions.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Senior ML Infra Engineer, Aurora Analytics
samir@auroradata.com

Samir — I attached the intake form and a lightweight runbook so Ben can annotate. Also: if you could send a short histogram of sequence lengths (avg + 95th) that will speed the sizing.

- Tue 2027-05-11 11:00–11:30

Neha

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — quick throughput/latency triage

Hi all — thanks for the context, Samir. Short answers and a proposed agenda below.

Quick technical notes:
- Llama-2-70B (quantized) at ~1.5k tokens/sec sustained is near the top end of what we'd size for a single dedicated pool depending on sequence length and batch tolerance. With aggressive batching + KV cache warm, p95 <150ms is achievable on an optimized GPU fleet but likely requires multi-GPU partitioning or a higher-slot Dedicated plan.
- Distilled 13B will be far cheaper and can hit targets with smaller pools; tradeoff is model fidelity.

What I need from Aurora before the demo:
1) Sequence length histogram (avg, 50/90/95/99) — helps pick kernel & batch size.
2) Typical prompt+response token mix (percent of generation vs prompt).
3) Whether you need strict per-request tail latency SLAs or a best-effort p95 goal.

Proposed demo agenda (30m):
- 5m: Intros + scope (Neha/Lauren)
- 10m: Workload profile & sizing (Samir + Ben)
- 10m: Live throughput / latency demo on a representative model variant
- 5m: Next steps: trial sizing, quote, and timeline

I attached a short capacity playbook that outlines recommended GPU configs and fallback options. For scheduling, Tue 11:00 PST works for me.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity-playbook.pdf

Thanks Ben — I pulled the histograms. Quick answers:
- Avg seq length: ~64 tokens; 95th percentile ~420 tokens; occasional long-run tail up to ~2k tokens but rare
- Prompt vs generation: ~30% prompt, 70% generation on average
- We’re aiming for p95 SLA (customer-facing feature), but can accept short p99 spikes during batch windows

Tue 2027-05-11 11:00 PST works — confirm and I’ll block the calendar.

—Samir
